ActorAssignment.description: An actor assignment associates a person with an action. It is an object assumption so that the attribution can be annotated with a belief about its certainty.

Agent.description: A person or a group: a pianist, an editor, a publisher, a manufacturer, a library.

name.description: The name, e.g. "Grünfeld, Alfred", "Wien", "M. Welte & Söhne".

role.description: The role of the agent in the context of the edition.

AgentRole.description: The role an agent plays in the context of the edition.

AnyArgumentation.description: An argumentation can be either a plain argumentation, a meaning comprehension, an inference, or a belief adoption.

AnyFeature.description: The union of all physical feature types that can appear on a roll: holes (perforations), writings (labels, annotations), marks (pencil, ink), and glued-on patches (paper, tape).

AnySymbol.description: A symbol can be either a note, an expression, or a text. Notes and expressions are perforations; texts are carried by writings.

Argumentation.description: An argumentation provides reasons for a belief and may be associated with a person carrying out that argumentation.

actor.description: The person who carried out this activity.

note.description: A free-text note providing additional context.

@type.description: The type discriminator for this object.

Belief.description: A belief is a temporal object and associates a proposition (i.e. a statement) with a certainty. It comes into existence through argumentations (reasons).

certainty.description: The level of certainty associated with this belief.

reasons.description: The argumentations providing reasons for this belief.

@id.description: A unique identifier for this object.

@type.description: The type discriminator for this object.

BeliefAdoption.description: A belief adoption adopts someone else's belief. This type is used to indicate e.g. knowledge through private communication or from secondary literature.

actor.description: The person who carried out this activity.

note.description: A note describing the source of the adopted belief, e.g. a bibliographic reference or personal communication.

@type.description: The type discriminator for this object.

Certainty.description: Certainty levels for beliefs, ranging from 'true' to 'false' and some values in between.

CollationTolerance.description: Tolerance used in collation of roll copies: the acceptable deviation at either end when aligning features across copies.

toleranceEnd.description: Tolerance at the end position of a feature.

toleranceStart.description: Tolerance at the start position of a feature.

DateAssignment.description: When something happened, as far as the edition can state it: the day it falls `within`, or the bounds it lies between. A bound nobody can give is left out, so `after` alone says "not before".

Derivation.description: A derivation names the version another one was derived from, together with the tolerance the two were collated at. How precisely the copies put a symbol depends on what they are and on how their features were obtained, so the tolerance can differ from derivation to derivation.

Edit.description: A set of edits transforms a version of a roll into another version. Edits insert or delete symbols, or both (= replace). Edits may be motivated by a given set of reasons, e.g. to add an additional accent or to correct an error. If an edit is the interpretation of a metamark, such as a pencil mark, this should be made explicit using a meaning comprehension on the `@annotation` field.

@annotation.description: An optional annotation expressing a belief about this assumption. Uses the JSON-LD-star `@annotation` mechanism to attach epistemic metadata (certainty and reasons) to any triple.

belief.description: The belief held about the annotated statement.

delete.description: References (by `@id`) to the symbols to be deleted by this edit.

insert.description: The symbols to be inserted by this edit.

motivation.description: A textual description of the motivation for this edit, referencing a motivation defined in the version's motivations list.

@id.description: A unique identifier for this object.

@type.description: The type discriminator for this object.

EditType.description: The type of editorial change applied to a symbol or set of symbols. Classifies the nature of the edit, e.g. whether it corrects an error, adds an accent, shifts a note, or shortens/prolongs a perforation.

copies.description: The physical roll copies on which this edition is based.

creation.description: Information about the creation of this edition, including publisher and publication date.

license.description: The license under which the edition is published.

roll.description: The roll which is edited in this edition.

tempoAdjustment.description: An optional tempo adjustment for playback of the roll, annotatable with a belief about its correctness.

versions.description: The different versions of the roll on which this edition is based.

editors.description: The persons who prepared the edition, each with the part they took in the editorial work. An edition written before this field existed carries none.

publicationDate.description: The date on which the edition was published.

publisher.description: The person or institution responsible for publishing the edition.

Editor.description: A person who took part in preparing the edition.

name.description: The name, e.g. "Grünfeld, Alfred", "Wien", "M. Welte & Söhne".

role.description: The part this person took in the editorial work.

EditorialRole.description: The part an editor took in the editorial work.

Expression.description: An expression symbol, representing a perforation on the roll that governs dynamics, pedaling, or mechanical functions of the reproducing piano. Each expression has a scope (bass or treble) and a specific expression type.

after.description: A perforation whose onset this one follows when the roll is performed, the counterpart of `before`. This points to the perforation by its `@id`.

alignedWith.description: In piano rolls, perforations are often aligned with other perforations, e.g. a "crescendo off" might be logically aligned to the start of a note perforation. This points to the perforation by its `@id`.

before.description: A perforation whose onset this one precedes when the roll is performed, without saying by how much: a "crescendo off" ends before the note it leads to begins, even where the copies disagree on it. Where the measurement has it so, nothing moves; where it does not, this one is placed before the reference as far as the copies that agree put it. This points to the perforation by its `@id`.

carriers.description: References to the physical features (e.g. holes) on the roll copies that carry this symbol. Since the association might be debatable, it can be annotated. There might be e.g. doubts about the meaning and correct transcription of a feature on a physical roll. This points to a feature by its `@id`.

expressionType.description: The command the perforation gives, named as the reproducing system of the roll names it: "SustainPedalOn", "ForzandoOff" and so on for the Welte-Mignon T-100. The tracker bar of the system lists the values it reads.

pairedWith.description: The perforation this one forms a pair with, e.g. a "forzando on" with its "forzando off". Any two perforations may be paired. The distance between the two is fixed: whatever displaces the one displaces the other. The relation is symmetric and is stated on one side only. This points to the perforation by its `@id`.

scope.description: Whether this expression applies to the bass or treble register.

@id.description: A unique identifier for this object.

@type.description: The type discriminator for this object.

ExpressionScope.description: The scope of an expression perforation, indicating whether it applies to the bass or treble register of the piano.

FeatureSource.description:
The capture by which a copy's features became data: what they were read from, who read them, on what device, with what software and when. It states where the numbers of the edition come from and says nothing about the state of the paper, which is a condition.

What is not known is left out. A reader is told about the gap by `reservationsAbout`, which works out what a copy cannot vouch for from what it states here.

device.description: The make and model of the scanner, camera or player the capture ran on.

instrument.description: The instrument the copy was played on, where the capture is a recording of it.

kind.description: What the features were read from.

note.description: A free-text note providing additional context.

output.description: The file the capture produced, where it has an address.

software.description: The software the capture ran, each with its version.

GluedOn.description: A piece of material (paper or tape) glued onto the roll surface. Glued-on features are typically used to cover perforations (for corrections) or to reinforce damaged areas. They may themselves carry other features such as writings or additional holes.

condition.description: This can be used e.g. to indicate a perforation which is torn out or in any other way damaged.

depiction.description: IIIF region pointing to a depiction of this feature in the scan.

features.description: A glued-on feature itself may carry other features. Nested features do not need to be positioned explicitly.

horizontal.description: Horizontal span of the feature on the roll.

material.description: The material of the glued-on feature.

vertical.description: Vertical span of the feature on the roll.

@id.description: A unique identifier for this object.

@type.description: The type discriminator for this object.

Hole.description: A hole (perforation) in the roll paper. Holes are the primary carriers of musical information on piano rolls, as they trigger notes and expression controls when passing over the tracker bar. A punched hole is a human-made feature: CRM counts "the information encoding features on mechanical or digital carriers" among the features purposely created by human activity.

condition.description: This can be used e.g. to indicate a perforation which is torn out or in any other way damaged.

depiction.description: IIIF region pointing to a depiction of this feature in the scan.

horizontal.description: Horizontal span of the feature on the roll.

pattern.description: The punching pattern of the hole. Regular holes have evenly-spaced bridges, accelerating holes have decreasing bridge widths, and staggering holes do not align in rows across the tracks, the mark of an asynchronous perforator with a separate driver for each punch (Phillips 2016, p. 112).

vertical.description: Vertical span of the feature on the roll.

@id.description: A unique identifier for this object.

@type.description: The type discriminator for this object.

HorizontalSpan.description: Describes the horizontal extent of a feature on the roll, measured in millimeters from the beginning of the roll. The `from` value is the start position and `to` is the end position.

from.description: The start position of the feature in millimeters from the beginning of the roll.

to.description: The end position of the feature in millimeters from the beginning of the roll.

unit.description: The unit of measurement for horizontal positions. Always 'mm' (millimeters).

Inference.description: An inference draws a conclusion from given premises.

actor.description: The person who carried out this activity.

note.description: A free-text note providing additional context.

premises.description: References (by `@id`) to the beliefs from which the conclusion is drawn.

used.description: References (by `@id`) to what the inference worked on besides beliefs, such as the versions it compared or the analysis output it cites.

@type.description: The type discriminator for this object.

KeeperAssignment.description: The keeper a copy is held by, as an object assumption, so that the statement can carry the belief it rests on and the reasons for it.

Mark.description: A visible mark on the roll, such as a pencil circle, an ink stroke, or other non-textual annotation. What a mark was meant to say is a reading of it (crminf:I16 Meaning Comprehension) rather than a property of the feature, so its shape is not stated here.

ProductionEvent.description: Describes the production of a roll copy: the manufacturer, the paper used, the date, and the system and paper speed the copy was cut for.

company.description: The company that produced the roll copy (e.g. "M. Welte & Söhne").

date.description: The date of production, if known.

paper.description: The paper the roll copy was cut on.

speed.description: The paper speed the copy was cut for. A copy cut from the same master for another speed comes out longer or shorter than the roll it is aligned with by the ratio of the speeds, which is what the alignment then measures.

system.description: The reproducing system the copy was cut for. Left out, it is the roll's own; a Licensee re-cut of a T-100 roll names the Licensee here. A system the type vocabulary knows carries the IRI of its concept as `id`.

RecordingEvent.description: Describes the event of recording and documents the persons involved in the process (e.g. pianist), the place, and the date of the recording.

created.description: The version of the roll which was created in the recording. Since it is usually not handed down, this is an optional property.

date.description: The recording date of the roll. This is a date assignment so that we can state e.g. the catalogue or the roll label which indicates the date of the recording.

place.description: The place where the recording took place.

recorded.description: Documents the performance which was recorded.

pianist.description: The pianist who gave the recorded performance.

playing.description: This property should point to a standard URI, e.g. the GND.

Roll.description: The abstract concept of a roll, identified by its catalogue number.

catalogueNumber.description: The catalogue number of the roll.

RollConditionAssignment.description: An assignment of a condition (general or paper-stretch) to a roll copy, annotatable with a belief about its certainty.

RollCopy.description: A physical copy of a roll, held at a specific location. Each roll copy has its own set of features, measurements, conditions, and modifications. Multiple copies of the same roll may exist across different archives or collections.

carries.description: The versions this copy is held to carry, where its features are not read into symbols, as for a copy known only from a recording. Each statement carries the belief it rests on.

conditions.description: Condition assessments of this roll copy (e.g. paper stretch, general wear). Each condition is an assumption annotatable with a belief.

features.description: The physical features found on this copy, with shift and stretch already applied when `ops` says so.

keeper.description: The institution or person holding this copy. Left out where it is not known, as for a copy known only from a recording. An object assumption, so that a keeper read off a file header or adopted from a letter can say where it comes from. Who held the copy before is not stated here: P50 names the current keeper.

measurements.description: Physical measurements of this roll copy, including dimensions, punch diameter, hole separation, margins, shift corrections, and information about the measuring software.

dimensions.description: The physical dimensions of the roll.

height.description: The total height (length) of the roll.

holeSeparation.description: The distance between adjacent tracker bar holes, in the unit the scan was measured in.

margins.description: The margins on the treble and bass sides of the roll. Not exported to RDF.

measuredBy.description: Information about the software used to take the measurements.

date.description: The date on which the measurements were taken.

software.description: The name of the measurement software.

version.description: The version of the measurement software.

punchDiameter.description: The average diameter of punched holes.

scale.description: The factor this copy's features were scaled by to align them with the others. What it is put down to is stated apart: a paper-stretch condition, or the speed the copy was cut for. Not exported to RDF.

scanResolution.description: The resolution this copy's scan was read at, along the roll. It is what the measurements given in pixels are to be read against, and what every conversion between a place in the scan and one on the paper goes through. A scanner may read across the roll at another resolution, which the analysis files do not state.

shift.description: The shift applied to align this copy with the others. Not exported to RDF.

trackCalibration.description: Relates this copy's scan to the tracker bar: how the scanning software's hole numbering was shifted onto the bar, and where the track grid sits in the image. Not exported to RDF.

ops.description: A list of operations that have been applied to this copy's features (e.g. 'shifted', 'stretched') to normalize measurements for comparison with other copies. Not exported to RDF.

production.description: The production event that created this roll copy.

readFrom.description: What this copy's features were read from. A copy that states no source is one whose features reached the edition by a way that was not written down.

scan.description: The scan URL or IIIF URL of the roll.

siglum.description: A short siglum to identify the copy, e.g. "St1" or "Wi1": letters for the collection the copy was read in, and a number counting the copies of the roll held there. A copy without one is named by its keeper.

@id.description: A unique identifier for this object.

@type.description: The type discriminator for this object.

Shift.description: A shift correction applied to a roll copy to align it with other copies. The shift is defined as horizontal (along the roll length, in mm) and vertical (across tracks).

Software.description: Software a capture ran, such as the transcriber that read a recording into notes or the emulator that wrote a MIDI file.

version.description: The release, or the model checkpoint of a transcriber.

Text.description: A textual symbol, e.g. a label or annotation found on the roll.

carriers.description: References to the physical features (e.g. holes) on the roll copies that carry this symbol. Since the association might be debatable, it can be annotated. There might be e.g. doubts about the meaning and correct transcription of a feature on a physical roll. This points to a feature by its `@id`.

text.description: The text content of the symbol.

@id.description: A unique identifier for this object.

@type.description: The type discriminator for this object.

Track.description: A position across the roll, numbered as the tracker bar does.

TrackCalibration.description:
Relates a scan to the tracker bar it was read with.

Scanning software numbers the hole columns it finds by their position in the image, so its numbering is offset by however far the roll lay from the edge of the scanner bed. Calibrating means finding that offset, usually from a landmark such as the rewind perforation.

    column      = offset + scannerTrack * separation     trackerBar  = scannerTrack + shift

offset.description: Image column of the scanning software's track 0.

separation.description: Distance between the centres of adjacent tracks.

shift.description: Added to the scanning software's numbering to reach the tracker bar.

Version.description: A version is defined by the sum of edits applied to the version it is based on. What it is called is not stored with it: `siglaOf` reads the sigla off the stemma, so that a label never outlives the arrangement it describes.

basedOn.description: The versions this one is held to derive from, each under the belief it rests on. The text is read against the principal one (`principalDerivationOf`); the others stand as hypotheses, such as a contamination. A version that names none represents the mother roll.

creation.description: The act that made this version, where it is known: who carried it out, when, and by what rule.

edits.description: The list of edits that, applied to the base version, produce this version. A hypothetical version whose changes nobody can state leaves it out; it then reads as the version it derives from.

motivations.description: A collection of motivations used in this version's edits.

siglum.description: A label a document carries from before the sigla were computed. Nothing should write one here and nothing should show one: what a version is called comes from `siglaOf`.

system.description: The reproducing system this version is coded for. One roll was often issued for several of them, and a version is a reading in one system's words: its expression types are that system's vocabulary and its notes sit on that bar's positions. A system the type vocabulary knows carries the IRI of its concept as `id`, from which the export takes the system's own context.

@id.description: A unique identifier for this object.

@type.description: The type discriminator for this object.

VersionCreation.description:
How a version was made, where that is known and worth stating.

A roll issued for another system was re-punched by an editor of the publisher's, and that was an editorial act rather than a conversion: Lawson names Kähle as the man who corrected second masters for the green system. The rule he worked by is the procedure named here, and the version's edits carry it out, so the mechanical part of a transfer is stated once instead of being spelled out per note.

actor.description: Who carried the act out. An `ObjectAssumption`, so an attribution can carry the belief it rests on and the reasons for it.

procedure.description: The rule followed, as a term of the vocabulary: the notes stand at their pitch, the expression is re-spelled in the other system's words.

VerticalSpan.description: Describes the vertical extent of a feature on the roll, measured in track numbers. Track numbers correspond to positions on the tracker bar.

from.description: The start track number of the feature.

to.description: The end track number, if the feature spans multiple tracks. If omitted, the feature occupies a single track.

unit.description: The unit of measurement for vertical positions.

Writing.description: A piece of writing found on the roll, such as a label, catalogue number, or annotation. Writings have a method of production and a transcription of their content.

condition.description: This can be used e.g. to indicate a perforation which is torn out or in any other way damaged.

depiction.description: IIIF region pointing to a depiction of this feature in the scan.

horizontal.description: Horizontal span of the feature on the roll.

method.description: The method by which this writing was produced (e.g. through print, handwriting, or stamping).

transcription.description: A transcription of the text content of the writing. This is an object assumption so that the transcription can be annotated with a belief about its correctness.

vertical.description: Vertical span of the feature on the roll.

@id.description: A unique identifier for this object.

@type.description: The type discriminator for this object.

WritingMethod.description: The method by which a writing was produced on the roll: printed, handwritten, or stamped.
